turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class.
Okay. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so tell me who decided on the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
Seventeen, and he lives at home with me. That's why your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark goes in. Nobody called me, Hale.
A grocery store. Why does that matter to you, Hale? I'm still waiting to hear who decided on the zero.
When did his dad move out?
That's not your business, Hale, and it has nothing to do with a zero on an essay. Is there a document, or am I going to the principal's office?
And what day was the zero entered?
Tuesday, November 3. You entered it, Hale, so you tell me why nobody called me before it went in.
What do you know about his essay so far?
Only that it's Owen's Hamlet essay, that a checker flagged it, and that he wrote it himself. That's a machine's guess, Hale. What else do you have?
